Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on Surah 110, verses 1–3:

It was revealed at Mina during the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajj al-Wada'). It is counted as a Medinan surah. It is the last surah to be revealed, and it has 3 verses. "It was revealed after al-Tawba (Surah 9)."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Idha ja'a﴾ ("When... comes") is in the accusative case, governed by ﴿sabbih﴾ ("glorify"), and refers to the future. The announcement of this before it happened is one of the signs of prophethood. It is related that it was revealed on the days of al-Tashriq at Mina during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

If you ask: what is the difference between ﴿al-nasr﴾ ("help/victory") and ﴿al-fath﴾ ("conquest"), that the one is conjoined to the other? I say: al-nasr is relief and manifestation over the enemy. From it comes the saying, "Allah helped (nasara) the land," meaning He gave it rain. Al-fath is the conquest of cities. The meaning is: the help of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over the Arabs, or over the Quraysh and the conquest of Makka. It has also been said: it refers to the genus of Allah's help to the believers and the conquest of the lands of polytheism for them. The conquest of Makka took place ten nights after the month of Ramadan had passed, in the eighth year (AH), and with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were ten thousand from the Emigrants and the Helpers and groups of the Arab tribes. He stayed there fifteen nights, then went out against Hawazin. When he entered it, he stood at the door of the Ka'ba, and then said: "There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. He has fulfilled His promise, helped His servant, and defeated the confederates alone." Then he said: "O people of Makka, what do you think I will do with you?" They said: "Good. A noble brother and the son of a noble brother." He said: "Go, for you are the freed ones (al-tulaqa')." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set them free. [Ibn Ishaq related it in his Sira. Al-Bukhari related from Ibn 'Abbas that "the Prophet (ﷺ) left Makka in Ramadan," and in the narrative: "He came upon it on the thirteenth night of Ramadan." In al-Dala'il, through Ibn Ishaq from al-Zuhri and others, it says: "It was conquered ten nights before the end (of Ramadan)."] Allah had enabled him over their necks by force, and they had become spoils (fay') for him. For this reason the people of Makka were called the freed ones. Then they pledged allegiance to him for Islam.

﴿Fi dini Allah﴾ ("in the religion of Allah") means: in the religion of Islam, the creed for which there is no other religion that may be attributed to Him besides it. ﴿Wa man yabtaghi ghayr al-Islam dinan fa-lan yuqbila minh﴾ ("And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him").

﴿Afwaja﴾ ("in multitudes") means: dense groups. The whole tribe would enter it together, after they had been entering it one by one and two by two.

It is related from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him) that he wept one day, and it was said to him [the phrase "fa-qila lahu" is perhaps: "it was said to him about that." (Editor's note)]. He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'People entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and they will leave it in multitudes.'" [Ahmad, Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh and al-Tha'labi related it through al-Awza'i: "Abu 'Ammar told me, a neighbour of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah told me, he said: 'I came from a journey, and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah came to me and greeted me. I began to tell him about the division of the people and what they had innovated. He began to weep, then said: I heard...' and he mentioned it." It has a witness from Abu Hurayra in al-'Ayn in al-Mustadrak.]

It has also been said that by "the people" is meant the people of Yemen. Abu Hurayra said: When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allahu akbar! The help of Allah and the conquest have come, and the people of Yemen have come: a people whose hearts are tender. Faith is Yamani, understanding is Yamani, and wisdom is Yamani." [Ibn Mardawayh related it through 'Abd al-Razzaq, who told us: Hisham ibn Hassan related from Muhammad ibn Sirin from him. Its origin is in Muslim, without what is at its beginning. It has a witness in Ibn Hibban and al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.] And he said: "I find the breath (nafas) of your Lord from the direction of Yemen." [Al-Tabarani related it in al-Awsat and Musnad al-Shamiyyin through Jarir ibn 'Uthman from Shabib ibn Rawh from Abu Hurayra, in a hadith beginning: "Faith is Yamani." Its chain is not objectionable. It has a witness from the hadith of Salama ibn Nufayl al-Sakuni in Musnad al-Bazzar, al-Tabarani's al-Kabir and al-Bayhaqi's al-Asma'. Its chain contains Ibrahim ibn Sulayman al-Aftas. Al-Bazzar said: "He is not well known."]

From al-Hasan: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makka, the Arabs came to one another and said: "Since he has prevailed over the people of the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram), there is no power to resist him. Allah had protected them from the companions of the Elephant and from everyone who wanted them." So they entered Islam in multitudes without fighting.

Ibn 'Abbas read: ﴿Fath Allah wa al-nasr﴾ ("the conquest of Allah and the help"). It was also read: ﴿yadkhulun﴾ ("they enter"), in the passive form (yudkhalun is not the reading here; it is said to be read in the passive voice). If you ask: what is the grammatical position of ﴿yadkhulun﴾? I say: it is in the accusative, either as a circumstantial state (hal), taking ﴿ra'ayta﴾ to mean "you saw" or "you knew," or it is a second object if it means "you knew."

﴿Fa-sabbih bi-hamdi rabbika﴾ ("So glorify your Lord with His praise"): say "Subhan Allah," praising Him. That is, be amazed at Allah's facilitation of what did not occur to you or to anyone, that someone would overcome the people of the Sacred Precinct; and praise Him for His doing. Or: remember Him, glorifying and praising, increasing in His worship and in extolling Him, because of the increase of His blessings upon you. Or: pray to Him.

Umm Hani related that when the door of the Ka'ba was opened, he prayed the forenoon prayer (salat al-duha) eight rak'as. [I have not found it in this form: its apparent meaning suggests that he prayed inside the Ka'ba. In the Sahihayn, from the hadith of Umm Hani: "On the day of the conquest of Makka, the Prophet (ﷺ) bathed in her house and prayed eight rak'as." Abu Dawud related it with the wording: "The Prophet (ﷺ) prayed the voluntary forenoon prayer, eight rak'as, giving the salam after every two rak'as." Its chain is sound. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shayba, al-Tabarani, Ibn Hibban, Abu Ya'la, al-Bayhaqi, al-Hakim and al-Tabari related it through more than thirty routes, and none of them mentioned this addition.]

From 'A'isha: the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to say often before his death: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance." [Agreed upon; the wording is Muslim's.]

The command to seek forgiveness along with glorification completes the command to that which is the foundation of the religion: combining obedience with guarding against disobedience. And so that his being commanded to this, despite his infallibility (ismah), would be a kindness (lutf) to his community. And because seeking forgiveness is humility before Allah and lowering of the self, it is itself an act of worship.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed I seek forgiveness a hundred times in a day and a night." [Muslim related it from the hadith of al-Aghar al-Muzani.]

It is related that when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family) recited it to his companions, they rejoiced, and al-'Abbas wept. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What makes you weep, O uncle?" He said: "Your soul has been announced to you (nu'iyat ilayka nafsuka)." He said: "It is indeed as you say." [Al-Tha'labi related it from Muqatil, and his chain to him is apart from the book.] He lived two years after that, and was not seen laughing or joyful.

It has also been said that it was Ibn 'Abbas who said that, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This youth has been given much knowledge." [I have not found it.]

It is related that when it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon and said: "Indeed a servant was given the choice by Allah between this world and meeting Him, and he chose meeting Allah." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) understood, and said: "We ransom you with our souls, our wealth, our fathers and our children." [Agreed upon. Its origin is from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, without its beginning about it being at the time of the revelation of the surah. Indeed, it contains what indicates that this was at the end of his life, and its revelation was at the end of his life without dispute.]

From Ibn 'Abbas: 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) used to bring him close and admit him with the people of Badr. 'Abd al-Rahman said: "Will you admit this youth with us, when among our sons there are those like him?" [Al-Bukhari related it from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas with this meaning; it does not specify 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf. Al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak and erred. Al-Bazzar related it and its last wording agrees with the last wording of the author.] 'Umar said: "He is among those whom you know." Ibn 'Abbas said: So one day he admitted them, and admitted me with them. He asked them about the saying of Allah, ﴿Idha ja'a nasru Allah﴾, and I do not think he asked them except on my account. Some of them said: "Allah commanded His Prophet, when victory was granted to him, to seek His forgiveness and turn to Him." I said: "It is not so; rather, his soul was announced to him." 'Umar said: "I know of it nothing except what you know," then said: "How do you blame me for it, after what you have seen?"

From the Prophet (ﷺ): he called Fatima (may Allah be pleased with her) and said: "O my daughter, indeed my soul has been announced to me." She wept, so he said: "Do not weep, for you will be the first of my family to join me." [Al-Bayhaqi related it at the end of al-Dala'il and Ibn Mardawayh through the narration of Hilal ibn Khabbab from 'Ikrima from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "When ﴿Idha ja'a nasru Allah wa al-fath﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called Fatima and said to her: 'Indeed my soul has been announced to me,' and she wept. He said to her: 'Be patient, for you will be the first of my family to join me.' Then one of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her..." The hadith, and its witness is in the Sahihayn from the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, through the narration of Masruq from her, at length.]

From Ibn Mas'ud: this surah is called the Surah of Farewell (Surat al-Tawdi'). ﴿Kana tawwaban﴾ ("He has always been Relenting") means: in the past times, since the creation of those under obligation, He has been relenting toward them when they seek forgiveness. So every one who seeks forgiveness should expect the like of that.

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites the surah ﴿Idha ja'a nasru Allah﴾ is given a reward like that of one who witnessed with Muhammad the day of the conquest of Makka." [Al-Tha'labi and al-Wahidi and Ibn Mardawayh related it with the chain to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]

[Ibn Mardawayh related it through 'Abd al-Razzaq, who told us: Hisham ibn Hassan related from Muhammad ibn Sirin from him. Its origin is in Muslim, without what is at its beginning. It has a witness in Ibn Hibban and al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.] And he said: "I find the breath (nafas) of your Lord from the direction of Yemen." [Al-Tabarani related it in al-Awsat and Musnad al-Shamiyyin through Jarir ibn 'Uthman from Shabib ibn Rawh from Abu Hurayra, in a hadith beginning: "Faith is Yamani." Its chain is not objectionable. It has a witness from the hadith of Salama ibn Nufayl al-Sakuni in Musnad al-Bazzar, al-Tabarani's al-Kabir and al-Bayhaqi's al-Asma'. Its chain contains Ibrahim ibn Sulayman al-Aftas. Al-Bazzar said: "He is not well known."]

From al-Hasan: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makka, the Arabs came to one another and said: "Since he has prevailed over the people of the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram), there is no power to resist him. Allah had protected them from the companions of the Elephant and from everyone who wanted them." So they entered Islam in multitudes without fighting.

Ibn 'Abbas read: ﴿Fath Allah wa al-nasr﴾ ("the conquest of Allah and the help"). It was also read: ﴿yadkhulun﴾ ("they enter"), in the passive form (yudkhalun is not the reading here; it is said to be read in the passive voice). If you ask: what is the grammatical position of ﴿yadkhulun﴾? I say: it is in the accusative, either as a circumstantial state (hal), taking ﴿ra'ayta﴾ to mean "you saw" or "you knew," or it is a second object if it means "you knew."

﴿Fa-sabbih bi-hamdi rabbika﴾ ("So glorify your Lord with His praise"): say "Subhan Allah," praising Him. That is, be amazed at Allah's facilitation of what did not occur to you or to anyone, that someone would overcome the people of the Sacred Precinct; and praise Him for His doing. Or: remember Him, glorifying and praising, increasing in His worship and in extolling Him, because of the increase of His blessings upon you. Or: pray to Him.

Umm Hani related that when the door of the Ka'ba was opened, he prayed the forenoon prayer (salat al-duha) eight rak'as. [I have not found it in this form: its apparent meaning suggests that he prayed inside the Ka'ba. In the Sahihayn, from the hadith of Umm Hani: "On the day of the conquest of Makka, the Prophet (ﷺ) bathed in her house and prayed eight rak'as." Abu Dawud related it with the wording: "The Prophet (ﷺ) prayed the voluntary forenoon prayer, eight rak'as, giving the salam after every two rak'as." Its chain is sound. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shayba, al-Tabarani, Ibn Hibban, Abu Ya'la, al-Bayhaqi, al-Hakim and al-Tabari related it through more than thirty routes, and none of them mentioned this addition.]

From 'A'isha: the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to say often before his death: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance." [Agreed upon; the wording is Muslim's.]

The command to seek forgiveness along with glorification completes the command to that which is the foundation of the religion: combining obedience with guarding against disobedience. And so that his being commanded to this, despite his infallibility (ismah), would be a kindness (lutf) to his community. And because seeking forgiveness is humility before Allah and lowering of the self, it is itself an act of worship.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed I seek forgiveness a hundred times in a day and a night." [Muslim related it from the hadith of al-Aghar al-Muzani.]

It is related that when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family) recited it to his companions, they rejoiced, and al-'Abbas wept. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What makes you weep, O uncle?" He said: "Your soul has been announced to you (nu'iyat ilayka nafsuka)." He said: "It is indeed as you say." [Al-Tha'labi related it from Muqatil, and his chain to him is apart from the book.] He lived two years after that, and was not seen laughing or joyful.

It has also been said that it was Ibn 'Abbas who said that, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This youth has been given much knowledge." [I have not found it.]

It is related that when it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon and said: "Indeed a servant was given the choice by Allah between this world and meeting Him, and he chose meeting Allah." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) understood, and said: "We ransom you with our souls, our wealth, our fathers and our children." [Agreed upon. Its origin is from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, without its beginning about it being at the time of the revelation of the surah. Indeed, it contains what indicates that this was at the end of his life, and its revelation was at the end of his life without dispute.]

From Ibn 'Abbas: 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) used to bring him close and admit him with the people of Badr. 'Abd al-Rahman said: "Will you admit this youth with us, when among our sons there are those like him?" [Al-Bukhari related it from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas with this meaning; it does not specify 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf. Al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak and erred. Al-Bazzar related it and its last wording agrees with the last wording of the author.] 'Umar said: "He is among those whom you know." Ibn 'Abbas said: So one day he admitted them, and admitted me with them. He asked them about the saying of Allah, ﴿Idha ja'a nasru Allah﴾, and I do not think he asked them except on my account. Some of them said: "Allah commanded His Prophet, when victory was granted to him, to seek His forgiveness and turn to Him." I said: "It is not so; rather, his soul was announced to him." 'Umar said: "I know of it nothing except what you know," then said: "How do you blame me for it, after what you have seen?"

From the Prophet (ﷺ): he called Fatima (may Allah be pleased with her) and said: "O my daughter, indeed my soul has been announced to me." She wept, so he said: "Do not weep, for you will be the first of my family to join me." [Al-Bayhaqi related it at the end of al-Dala'il and Ibn Mardawayh through the narration of Hilal ibn Khabbab from 'Ikrima from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "When ﴿Idha ja'a nasru Allah wa al-fath﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called Fatima and said to her: 'Indeed my soul has been announced to me,' and she wept. He said to her: 'Be patient, for you will be the first of my family to join me.' Then one of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her..." The hadith, and its witness is in the Sahihayn from the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, through the narration of Masruq from her, at length.]

From Ibn Mas'ud: this surah is called the Surah of Farewell (Surat al-Tawdi'). ﴿Kana tawwaban﴾ ("He has always been Relenting") means: in the past times, since the creation of those under obligation, He has been relenting toward them when they seek forgiveness. So every one who seeks forgiveness should expect the like of that.

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites the surah ﴿Idha ja'a nasru Allah﴾ is given a reward like that of one who witnessed with Muhammad the day of the conquest of Makka." [Al-Tha'labi and al-Wahidi and Ibn Mardawayh related it with the chain to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]
